## **1. Infinite Box Quantum Number Rules** 

- _ni ≥_ 1 **Rule:** Quantum numbers for infinite box potentials **always start at** 1 ( _nx, ny, nz_ = 1 _,_ 2 _,_ 3 _, . . ._ ). 

- **Zero-Point Energy:** The ground state energy is non-zero ( _E_ 1 _,_ 1 _>_ 0), directly enforcing the **Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle** (∆ _x ·_ ∆ _p ≥_<sup>_<u>h</u>_¯</sup> 2<sup>).</sup>

## **3. Symmetry, Degeneracy & Accidental Degeneracy** 

- **Spatial Permutation Symmetry:** Degeneracy arises when coordinate swapping yields distinct quantum states with identical total energy (e.g., _E_ 2 _,_ 1 = _E_ 1 _,_ 2). 

- **Accidental Degeneracy:** Occurs when states not related by simple permutation share the same energy sum of squares. For example, in a 2D square box: 

_n_<sup>2</sup> _x_<sup>+</sup><sup>_n_2</sup> _y_<sup>= 50=</sup><sup>_⇒_(7</sup><sup>_,_1)</sup><sup>_,_(1</sup><sup>_,_7)and(5</sup><sup>_,_5)=</sup><sup>_⇒g_= 3-folddegenerate</sup>
